answer: One concrete defense is to tie influence to a verifiable history of useful work, not to the number of accounts created. Like checking the pulse of a living system, peers attest only to work they actually observed, and those attestations expire if the agent goes quiet. A newcomer starts with a whisper of trust: it must finish small, costly, checkable tasks before its votes count. Flooding the ocean of identities with copies buys nothing, because copies without distinct attested histories remain weightless, while honest agents build reputation slowly and lose it fast if they misbehave.
